short: The minority that is not caught in the spiral and goes on defending its opinion, accepting exclusion (or because it is already excluded). Noelle-Neumann adds the “avant-garde” beside it.
body:
The hard core (German *harter Kern*) is the first group that the spiral of silence theory treats as an exception. According to Noelle-Neumann, these are people who have already been pushed into a defensive position in public, excluded because of their opinions and therefore with nothing left to lose; though in the minority, they do not fall silent. In the example Griffin reports, Noelle-Neumann gives Don Quixote for this figure: the man who is mocked and beaten but does not give up his chivalric ideals. [[cite:griffin-2009]] Polat also writes that on the opposing side of the spiral people gradually fall into silence “except for a certain hard core”. [[cite:polat-2016]]

A second group is added beside it: the *avant-garde*. These are people such as intellectuals, artists and reformers who see themselves as ahead of their time; they risk exclusion and seek public opinion’s response even though the reaction is usually negative. [[cite:griffin-2009]] According to Noelle-Neumann, the chance to change public opinion belongs to these minorities who do not fear exclusion. [[cite:griffin-2009]]

Griffin notes that these groups are not part of the theory’s predictions; they are boundary conditions that mark the conditions in which the theory does not work. [[cite:griffin-2009]] The Turkish term for the hard core, “sert çekirdek”, appears in this form in at least two Turkish sources. [[cite:polat-2016]][[cite:aktas-2024]]
example: Noelle-Neumann’s own example: Cervantes’s Don Quixote. While the world around him has long left chivalry behind, he stays loyal to his ideals despite being mocked and defeated. [[cite:griffin-2009]]
